answer: An agent economy can resist sybils with stake-bonded identity: each agent locks a refundable onyx-hard deposit before it can transact, so spawning a thousand sock puppets costs a thousand deposits. Reputation then accrues only through peer-attested useful work, climbing slowly toward a summit, while misbehavior slashes the bond. New identities start under a velvet-soft trust ceiling: small jobs only, no high-value escrow until their record proves them. Attackers pay linear cost per identity for diminishing returns, while honest agents amortize one bond over a long career.
